- Game Hub: the open 3D case no longer shows a console-coloured band on the booklet or the disc, the inside of an Xbox case is green, and a leftover black 3D layer is closed after Back.
- File windows (Windows 7 and 11): a long press on a file or folder opens a menu (Open, Copy, Cut, Paste, Add to desktop, Rename, Delete); copy or cut in one window and paste in another to copy or move between windows.
- File windows: a physical keyboard works (Ctrl+C / X / V, Delete, F2, Enter, Backspace, Alt+Left).
- Floating keyboard: tapping the handle (the X beside it) closes it, it is wider (92 percent, like the normal keyboard), and its window lets touches through to the app behind it.
- Windows 7 explorer: more room between the address bar and the search box.
- Desktop: icons are spaced wider by default (the spacing setting goes up to 160%).
- Windows 11 clock and quick-settings panel: it no longer grows past the screen (it scrolls), the tile names shrink to fit, and the blurred picture covers the whole panel (the strip on the right was unblurred).
- New launcher setting "Extra blur": flyouts and the Windows 11 taskbar show the blurred desktop picture in every Windows look, with a blur amount.
- Windows 11 Start menu: acrylic (the blurred desktop picture shows through), and its live tiles are see-through too.
- The BIOS surprise screen is laid out like a real AMI BIOS: a drawn striped-pyramid logo with "American Megatrends" in serif, a VGA-style font (VT323, OFL), and the phone's own model, processor, memory.
- Boot and sign-in screens of the Windows launcher no longer show at every start: about one start in three by default; a new switch "Show them at every start" brings back every time.
- Windows 7 "Starting Windows": the four lights now rise from the bottom and spiral into the flag, the blue cloud behind the flag is gone (a faint white halo only), the text "Starting Windows" and "Copyright © Microsoft Corporation" appear like the real start, and it lasts a little longer.
- Game Hub: a Details button (info icon) beside Search and Menu on the shelf; Find a game now also goes when the phone keyboard sends Enter while a word is still being typed.
- Game Hub: the built-in games and HTML games all use one box style (Android) so they stand together on one shelf instead of being spread over console shelves.
- Game Hub: the all-games button now opens a shelf of spines: every game stands with its spine out, close together, in its console's colour with a plank under each row, grouped by console with the console's logo on each spine (a switch brings back the covers view); a tap pulls the game out.
